expectations.real_bar: Cloud growth at or above ~50% with management stating that the share of compute rented overseas is small or replaceable (T-Head/domestic) and reiterating that AI+cloud growth keeps accelerating; another adjusted-EPS miss is the base case and is tolerated.

next_guide.street_full_year: FY27/FY28 estimates stable over 90 days; FY28 EPS RMB61.65 per ADS (TIKR 2026-11-10, https://www.tikr.com/blog/alibaba-keeps-sliding-why-goldman-sachs-sees-68-upside)
next_guide.company_current_guide: Qualitative only: AI+cloud revenue growth 'will accelerate further in the coming quarters' and annualised AI product revenue approaching $10bn in the September quarter (2026-08-20 call, https://thenextweb.com/news/alibaba-ai-spending-profit-falls-75-percent-cloud); capex above the RMB380bn three-year plan hinted at the 2026-09-22 Apsara Conference (https://www.mobileworldlive.com/ai-cloud/alibaba-plots-ai-capex-hike/).
next_guide.basis: Same-quarter China AI-compute demand is strong (Baidu GPU cloud +191%), so the cloud-acceleration language is likely reiterated, but the Nov-16 BIS rule puts a 90-day licence clock on overseas capacity serving China firms, which is the main way the cloud guide could be softened; capex is more likely raised than cut.

findings.finding: The ADR is down 15.4% in 5 days, 17.75% in 20 days and ~34% from the $130.53 close after the last print (2026-08-20) to $85.88, at its 52-week low and below the lowest of 41 analyst targets ($96, average $184), while FY27/FY28 estimates were stable over 90 days; the drop is tied to a US chip-access policy story (HK -6.8% on 2026-11-12 vs Tencent -2.6%) rather than to company numbers, so the market's real bar into the print is low on fundamentals.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the 2026-08-20 print the ADR recovered an intraday -5.4% to close +1.3% on cloud strength despite a 21% EPS miss; no prior print found where it entered at a 52-week low after a policy-driven drop.
findings.why_not_priced: The price already holds the chip-policy fear; what is not priced is any relief if the release shows the compute exposure is small. If the market expected a fundamental miss, estimates would have been cut alongside the price; they were stable (TIKR) while the price fell ~30%.
findings.independence: Price path and target spread from TIKR; 52-week-low status and 5d/20d from the sealed baseline; HK -6.8% vs Tencent -2.6% on 2026-11-12 from https://www.tikr.com/blog/alibaba-slides-7-as-wus-promise-to-accelerate-further-runs-into-u-s-chip-curbs ; post-earnings drift -29.8% from https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/BABA

findings.finding: Baidu's Q3 2026 (reported 2026-11-16, same September quarter): AI Cloud Infra revenue +94% YoY to RMB8.2bn, GPU Cloud +191% YoY and +43% QoQ, external Qianfan token revenue +1,159% - China AI-compute rental demand accelerated sharply in the quarter Alibaba reports, supporting AI Cloud growth at or above the >50% the street expects (45% last quarter).
findings.link: Same product (rented GPU/AI cloud and model-as-a-service) in the same China market and quarter; Baidu AI Cloud Infra RMB8.2bn vs Alibaba AI Cloud & Compute RMB48.4bn in June, so Baidu is about a sixth of Alibaba's scale; Alibaba held ~23% China AI-cloud share vs Baidu lower (IDC H1 2025 per boerse-express).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Cloud is the line BABA trades on: on 2026-08-20 cloud +45% (fastest in 22 quarters) turned an intraday -5.4% into a +1.3% close despite an EPS miss.
findings.why_not_priced: Printed three days before Alibaba and during a week the stock fell on chip-access news; if read across, the cloud bar would be visibly rising in previews, but the only cloud bar found (SCMP >50%) predates it. Partly priced: the street already expects acceleration. Bar for cloud is single-sourced, so capped small.
findings.independence: Baidu release coverage also at https://www.plataformamedia.com/en/2026/11/16/baidu-announces-third-quarter-2026-results/ (same document). Independent: Alibaba's own guide of further acceleration (https://thenextweb.com/news/alibaba-ai-spending-profit-falls-75-percent-cloud).

findings.finding: Alibaba Cloud raised AI compute prices 5-34% (high-end GPU instances +25-34%, including its own Zhenwu 810E instances) effective 2026-04-18, with existing customers repricing at renewal, so the September quarter is the first quarter where renewals carry the higher price broadly.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Cloud line drove the 2026-08-20 close (+1.3% after -5.4% intraday).
findings.why_not_priced: Public since March and part of the June quarter already; the renewal lag means some of the uplift lands in the September quarter, but it is likely in models, so small.
findings.independence: Same price notice reported by https://techradar.com/pro/alibaba-cloud-bumps-prices-by-up-to-34-percent-due-to-ai-demand-and-hardware-costs (same document).

findings.finding: JD.com's Q3 2026 release (2026-11-17): New Businesses (incl. food delivery) operating loss narrowed to RMB9.6bn from RMB15.7bn (-39% YoY) and group marketing expenses fell 26.2%, evidence that the instant-commerce subsidy war eased in the September quarter, which should narrow Alibaba's quick-commerce losses YoY against a peak-loss comparison quarter.
findings.link: JD and Alibaba (Taobao Instant Commerce) are the two challengers to Meituan in the same China instant-commerce subsidy war; Alibaba quick-commerce revenue was RMB53.3bn in the June quarter (~48% of China e-commerce revenue).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Quick-commerce losses drove the 2025 drawdown; the street already models September-quarter EBITDA +129% YoY (TIKR), so a narrowing is largely inside expectations.
findings.why_not_priced: JD reported two days before Alibaba; consensus EBITDA of ~RMB40bn already assumes a large rebound, so only a beat on loss narrowing would move the stock. If priced beyond consensus, previews would flag quick-commerce upside; none found.
findings.independence: Consensus expectation of EBITDA roughly doubling from https://www.tikr.com/blog/alibaba-stock-is-down-nearly-27-in-2026-as-earnings-keep-missing-estimates-heres-what-the-next-report-has-to-show ; no Alibaba statement on quick-commerce losses for the quarter found.

findings.finding: China's online goods sales growth slowed from +4.6% YoY Jan-Jul to +3.8% Jan-Sep (implying roughly +2% in Aug-Sep) and +2.9% Jan-Oct, October retail sales rose 0.4% vs 0.8% expected, and Singles' Day platform GMV grew only 3.7% (Syntun), weighing on Taobao/Tmall customer management revenue (-7.5% YoY last quarter) and on December-quarter commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CMR fell 7.5% in the June quarter and the stock still closed up on cloud; CMR has not been the line that moved the last prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Public macro series; partly priced. It is a proxy (national online sales, not Alibaba's GMV), so small. If priced fully, CMR estimates would already be negative; consensus CMR not found.
findings.independence: Jan-Jul figure https://www.stats.gov.cn/english/PressRelease/202608/t20260819_1965078.html ; Oct data https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/chinese-retail-sales-oct-yy-04-vs-exp-08-prev-11 ; Singles' Day https://www.emarketer.com/content/price-wars-cautious-subdued-singles-day-2026 ; JD Retail +2.9% YoY in the same quarter (JD 6-K).

findings.finding: BIS issued an interim final rule on 2026-11-16 requiring a licence for any data centre worldwide serving China-headquartered firms above 12m TPP of compute, with 90 days for existing sites, plus licences for chip exports to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil; Alibaba is reported as the largest customer of Singapore's Megaspeed, so the 2026-11-19 call must say how much of the compute behind its 'accelerate further' cloud guide is rented overseas.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print with an equivalent supply question; on 2026-11-12 the report of the coming rule alone took the HK line -6.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: The rule itself is priced (the stock fell ~15% in a week). What is not priced is the company's quantification: if the overseas share is material, the cloud acceleration guide is cut, and the stock would not already be at a 52-week low if the market were certain it was immaterial. Two-sided, hence the wide range.
findings.independence: Megaspeed/Alibaba link: https://www.tikr.com/blog/alibaba-slides-7-as-wus-promise-to-accelerate-further-runs-into-u-s-chip-curbs (Bloomberg-sourced); Megaspeed denies wrongdoing (https://www.newsbytesapp.com/news/business/nvidia-linked-megaspeed-says-probes-found-no-illegal-chip-transfers/story). T-Head chips are outside the rule (TIKR).

findings.finding: At the 2026-09-22 Apsara Conference Eddie Wu set a 20GW data-centre target by 2032 and signalled spending above the RMB380bn three-year capex plan without a new figure, after June-quarter capex of RMB67.7bn (+75%) and free cash flow of -RMB44.7bn; a capex raise on the call is likely and is funded by the August HK$80bn placement.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-08-20 the capex/FCF burn drew an intraday -5.4% that the cloud number reversed; the placement on 2026-08-24 took the HK line -8.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: Signalled but not quantified; a number on the call is new. Financing question asked: the money buys AI capacity that same-quarter peer demand (Baidu GPU cloud +191%) corroborates, so the sign is only slightly negative (FCF and dilution), not distress.

findings.finding: The adjusted-EPS bar is disputed ($1.39 Benzinga, $1.42 one aggregator on 3 estimates, $1.63 Earnings Whispers with a whisper of $1.56 below it), and Alibaba has missed adjusted-EPS consensus in 5 of 5 reports, so an EPS miss is the base case and carries little reaction.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: HK shares -2.9% on the announcement day.
findings.why_not_priced: Announced and partly priced; the listing itself is after the window, only call commentary lands inside it.

lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar disputed: EPS $1.39-$1.63 across sources, cloud bar single-sourced): capped the cloud-dependent findings - Baidu read-across +0.8 -> +0.6, price-hike +0.3 -> +0.2 - and moved p_up 54 -> 53.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the HK$80bn placement funds AI capacity corroborated by peer demand, so the capex/financing finding shrank -0.5 -> -0.3.
Rule 6/9 (inside what the street already models: EBITDA +129%): JD quick-commerce read-across +0.7 -> +0.4.
Rule 5 (macro proxy small): online-retail macro finding -0.6 -> -0.5.
Rule 1/3 (policy overhang persists after the print): expectations finding +1.5 -> +1.2.
